original_question: Fix k in N. In every colouring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n with k+1 colours, determine whether there must exist a geodesic path between some antipodal pair of vertices that uses at most k colour changes.
target_in_paper: Section 8, Conjecture 8.4: the more-than-two-colours analogue of Leader and Long’s antipodal-geodesic conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly fixes k, uses k+1 edge colours, asks for existence of a geodesic path, requires the endpoints to be an antipodal pair of vertices of Q_n, and imposes the bound of at most k colour-changes. It also stays on the precise k+1-colour extension stated in the paper, rather than drifting to the earlier 2-colour variants or to non-geodesic paths.
missing_details: The paper states this as a conjecture/open problem, not as an established theorem.
To be fully stand-alone, the quantification over n should be explicit: for every n in N (or n >= 1).
Q_n should be defined as the n-dimensional hypercube with vertex set {0,1}^n and edges between vertices differing in exactly one coordinate.
‘Antipodal vertices’ should be defined explicitly as a pair x, x̄ that differ in all n coordinates.
‘Geodesic path’ should be defined explicitly as a shortest path in Q_n, equivalently a path that does not repeat any coordinate direction; between antipodal vertices such a path has length n.
‘Colour-change’ should be defined explicitly as an index where two consecutive edges on the path receive different colours.
The colouring is an arbitrary edge-(k+1)-colouring of Q_n; unlike the 2-colour discussion earlier in the section, there is no antipodal-colouring hypothesis here.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic phrase such as ‘for all sufficiently large m’ is relevant to this graph-theoretic problem.
refined_question: For each fixed k in N, is it true that for every n in N, every edge-colouring of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n with k+1 colours contains a geodesic path between some antipodal pair of vertices x and x̄ (that is, a shortest x-x̄ path in Q_n, equivalently one using each coordinate direction at most once) such that along this path the colours change at most k times?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 8 rather than any earlier section of the collection. The paper first recalls the 2-colour geodesic antipodal conjecture in Conjecture 8.1 and uses the surrounding text there to define ‘geodesic’ and explain the antipodal setting. It then explicitly says, ‘Another direction is the extension to colourings of the edges of Q_n with more than two colours. The analogue of Leader and Long’s conjecture for more than two colours would be the following,’ and states Conjecture 8.4. Your draft matches that statement essentially verbatim, with only minor stand-alone clarifications needed. The paper does not give an explicit equivalent reformulation of Conjecture 8.4 itself, so no alternate formulation should be supplied.
